newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng edges to record close, gains capped.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng edges to record close, gains capped.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index edged to its fourth straight record close on Monday, led by lagging conglomerates, but the index ended off the day's highs as other stocks suffered profit-taking and Japanese shares fell.
The Hang Seng rose 11.84 points, or 0.09 percent, to 13,868.24 after hitting a session high of 13,994.86. Turnover was HK$11.35 billion, down from Friday's HK$13.51 billion.

"People were buying laggards," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities. "In this recent rally we saw banks rally and property stocks rise but the conglomerates have not done anything," he said.
Shares in Swire Pacific rose HK$2.50 to HK$74.25 and Wheelock added HK$1.00 to HK$24.10.
Brokers said the Hang Seng had met with some resistance as it approached 14,000 points on Monday and was only likely to breach that level once it had been tested a few more times.
"It is still a big figure that people are trying to conquer," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
A drop in Japanese share prices on Monday also capped the market's gains, brokers said. The Nikkei 225 share average tumbled 609.70 points, or 3.37 percent, to 17,480.34.

"It looks like we have quite strong resistance at 14,000 so probably we will need to consolidate for a while for the market to get enough momentum to break through," said Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities.
But he said the downside was limited, with 13,650 to 13,700 points expected to be strong support.

"The chances are higher that it will break on the upside. The U.S. market is still quite bullish and also I do not think there is enough inflationary pressure to force the Fed to raise interest rates at its next meeting," Wong said.
"Corporate earnings will be quite good for 1996 and people will buy shares on expectations of good results," Wong added.

Souvenir maker Yip's Pota International Co Ltd ended its market debut at HK$1.90 compared with an issue price of HK$1.00 and printing firm Cheong Ming Holdings Ltd closed its first day of trading at HK$1.32 compared with an issue price of HK$1.00.
Banks were mixed. HSBC Holdings rose HK$1.00 to HK$184.00 but Bank of East Asia ended down HK$0.40 at HK$36.80.
CITIC Pacific fell HK$0.80 to HK$39.80. Tam said investors were switching out of the stock into other conglomerates.
